title: Quadratically Regularized Optimal Transport: Localization Bounds and Affine Case Analysis
claim: Empirically fitted scaling exponents track the theoretical prediction across dimensions, with a modest, systematic relative error that grows with dimension.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared x-axis dimension, shaded std bands, dashed reference
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the x-axis, dimension d from 100 to 1000. The left panel plots empirical beta against d. A dashed black line shows the theoretical prediction 1/(d+2) and falls steeply from about 0.010 to 0.001. Two solid lines with dots, blue for nonlinear Gauss-Seidel and orange for semismooth Newton, have translucent shaded std bands. They start below the theory line at small d and converge onto it at large d. The right panel plots relative error, (beta ratio − 1), for the same two solvers. A dashed zero line marks no error. Both curves rise from about −0.45 at d=100 to about +0.5 at d=1000, crossing zero near d=400–550. Wide shaded bands overlap. Captions (a) and (b) sit beneath the panels. The eye goes first to the dashed theory curve on the left.
caption: Affine Brenier scaling diagnostics across dimensions: fitted log-log slope $\widehat\beta$ (left) and relative error $(d+2)\widehat\beta-1$ (right). Error bars show $\pm1$ empirical standard deviation over $R=10$ random seeds.
abstract: Quadratic regularization has emerged as a potential alternative to the popular entropic regularization in computational optimal transport, offering the theoretical advantage of producing sparse couplings through its hinge density structure. Despite recent progress in one-dimensional settings and general upper bounds, fundamental questions about the localization rate of QOT optimizers around the Monge coupling have remained open. In this work, we establish a general lower bound showing that the support of the QOT optimizer cannot concentrate around the Monge graph faster than order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{d+2}}$ in the directed Hausdorff distance, matching the conjectured optimal exponent under standard regularity assumptions in \citet{wiesel2025sparsity}. We also show that the QOT value gap controls the mean-squared deviation $\mathbb E_{Ï_\varepsilon}\|y-T(x)\|^2$ by the scale of $\varepsilon^{\frac{2}{d+2}}$. As a corollary, in the affine Brenier regime, which includes Gaussian-to-Gaussian transport, we derive a sharp pointwise tube bound of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{d+2}}$ by reducing the problem to self-transport and applying recent self-transport sparsity results. Finally, we validate our theoretical bound with a synthetic experiment in high-dimensional settings.
